'''Richard Peter Stanley''' (born June 23, 1944) is an Emeritus Professor of Mathematics at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], and an Arts and Sciences Distinguished Scholar at the [[University of Miami]]. From 2000 to 2010, he was the [[Norman Levinson]] Professor of [[Applied mathematics|Applied Mathematics]] at MIT.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www-math.mit.edu/~rstan/minicv/index.html |title=Curriculum Vitae | last=Stanley |first=Richard |date=2017 |access-date=June 29, 2017}}</ref>   He received his Ph.D. at [[Harvard University]] in 1971 under the supervision of [[Gian-Carlo Rota]].<ref name="mg">{{mathgenealogy|id=18025}}</ref> He is an expert in the field of [[combinatorics]] and its applications to other mathematical disciplines.<ref name="schock"/>

== Contributions ==
{{Further|Chromatic symmetric function}}
Stanley is known for his two-volume book ''Enumerative Combinatorics'' (1986–1999).<ref>{{cite journal|author=Andrews, George E.|author-link=George Andrews (mathematician)|title=Review: ''Enumerative combinatorics, Volume 1'' by Richard P. Stanley|journal=Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. (N.S.)|year=1987|volume=17|issue=2|pages=360–365|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/bull/1987-17-02/S0273-0979-1987-15595-9/S0273-0979-1987-15595-9.pdf|doi=10.1090/s0273-0979-1987-15595-9|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=Gessel, Ira M.|title=Review: ''Enumerative combinatorics, Volume 2'' by Richard P. Stanley|journal=Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. (N.S.)|year=2002|volume=39|issue=1|pages=129–135|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/bull/2002-39-01/S0273-0979-01-00928-4/S0273-0979-01-00928-4.pdf|doi=10.1090/s0273-0979-01-00928-4|doi-access=free}}</ref> He is also the author of ''Combinatorics and Commutative Algebra'' (1983) and well over 200 research articles in mathematics.  He has served as thesis advisor to 60 doctoral students, many of whom have had distinguished careers in combinatorial research.<ref name="mg"/> [[Donald Knuth]] named Stanley as one of his combinatorial heroes in a 2023 interview.<ref name="Bhāvanā – Donald Knuth in conversation 2023">{{cite journal | title=The Dawn of Rigour in the Art of Programming | website=Bhāvanā – The mathematics magazine | publisher = The Bhavana Trust | volume = 7 | issue = 1 | date=January 2023 | url=https://bhavana.org.in/the-dawn-of-rigour-in-the-art-of-programming/ | access-date=2024-01-30}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
Stanley's distinctions include membership in the [[United States National Academy of Sciences|National Academy of Sciences]] (elected in 1995), the 2001 [[Leroy P. Steele Prize|Leroy P. Steele Prize for Mathematical Exposition]],<ref>[http://www.combinatorics.net/Words/Stanley/stanley-Steel.htm American Mathematical Society News Release: Richard P. Stanley Wins AMS Steele Prize], The Combinatorics Net, January 11, 2001, retrieved 2013-12-27.</ref> the 2003 [[Schock Prize]],<ref name="schock">[http://www.combinatorics.net/Words/Stanley/stanley-Schock.html Richard P. Stanley receives the 2003 Rolf Schock Prize in Mathematics by the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences], The Combinatorics Net, 2003, retrieved 2013-12-27.</ref>  a [[plenary lecture at the International Congress of Mathematicians]] (in [[Madrid]], [[Spain]]),<ref>[http://www.icm2006.org/proceedings/Vol_I/25.pdf Increasing and decreasing subsequences and their variants], R. P. Stanley, Proc. ICM, 2006.</ref> and election in 2012 as a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2013-08-05.</ref> In 2022 he was awarded the [[Leroy P. Steele Prize|Leroy P. Steele Prize for Lifetime Achievement]].<ref>[http://www.ams.org/news?news_id=6892 Leroy P. Steele Prize for Lifetime Achievement 2022]</ref>
